audit_report:
# TyraX2 SPR staging and object replay audit

Date: 2026-10-02. Scope: read-only architecture audit after 1.169.1; no hardware/emulator run, engine build, repository edit or performance claim.

## Decision

The next independently useful item is a source/publication audit and a bounded SPR-to-RAM prefix prototype. Do not introduce CALL/RET at the same time. The 1.169.1 runtime supplies the lifetime and central submission seams that were absent when S1 was proposed, but it does not resolve the old no-flush corruption. Existing immutable REF replay already provides much of the reference-title object replay idea. A literal CALL conversion is not justified by evidence of a missing benefit.

The safe first SPR experiment retains all existing cache flushes. It can establish transfer and lifetime correctness, and price staging overhead; it cannot establish a cache-flush saving. Dropping the global write-back is a separate gated experiment requiring a complete dirty-source inventory and explicit ordering proof.

## Established local evidence

* docs/tyrax2.md: ordinary runtime frames use one native VIF1 chain, one END and one presentation FINISH; two banks each own 1 MiB source snapshots and 128 KiB prefix storage. Overflow, unsupported input, compatibility and explicit synchronization can split/drain.
* vif1_queue.cpp: kNativeQwords=8192; prepareArena allocates 64-byte-aligned cached RAM. flushRecording finalizes, completes prior presentation, then invalidates the lazy flushedUpTo watermark or explicitly FlushCache(0)s in eager mode before enqueue. start calls FlushCache(0) before starting a newly dirty logical sequence. Lazy flush is on by default, ISR off required for syscall safety.
* frame_chain_arena.hpp: mutable/unregistered REF input is copied into bank-owned RAM; immutable registered REF spans are borrowed with reader-bank bits. This is an ownership model, not a cache publication model. Registration does not write back dirty bytes.
* frame_vif_writer.hpp: clean bounded CNT/REF records, reserved final END, rollback before submission. referencedVif and the RAM resolver exclude scratchpad references. All control words are initialized, unlike stock packet2 padding.
* stapip_qbuffer_renderer.cpp: queued per-bag uniforms are copied inline, including MVP; sendObjectData retains FLUSHE before absolute uniform overwrites and FLUSH before changed wrap state. Existing complete baked VIF streams replay with one REF, with per-package REF-run replay where visibility requires it. These arenas contain VIF bytes, not nested DMA subroutine chains; they already contain per-package MSCAL/MSCNT. A baked entry is keyed to the microprogram/address as well as content.
* Current validator and arena reject CALL/RET/NEXT and SPR references. Extending them requires new bounded traversal, ownership and TTE semantics, not just a new tag emitter.
* Local pinned ps2sdk headers expose fromSPR channel 8, toSPR channel 9, dma_channel_wait, dma_channel_send_normal, EE_SYNCL and SyncDCache. Installed SDK has headers/libraries, not those C/assembly implementation sources at the expected source paths. Exact chosen cache-range operation and barrier behavior still require implementation/manual review before a no-flush hardware candidate.
* Repo search found no current engine fromSPR/toSPR channel users or numeric scratchpad allocator; this is absence of an in-tree owner, not proof that all custom project VU code, libraries or interrupts never use it.

## What the failed S1 arm proved

The September 16 probe used uncached StaPip packets, retained flushing for known qbuffer-pool REF chains and verified uncached allocation. Uncached + flush was pixel-identical to the control. Removing flush corrupted 1,271 of 262,144 pixels, concentrated in a 14-row horizon band. The flush removal itself recovered 1.09 ms work including refill in that OLD immediate/queue architecture; writing stock packet2 uncached cost +7.55 ms.

It proved that making packet bytes uncached does not prove every DMA input visible and ordered. It did NOT distinguish an unflushed RAM REF writer from the flush's ordering effect. It did not prove SPR unsafe, identify a missing source, prove a particular SYNC instruction sufficient, or quantify the 1.169.1 one-prefix gain. Repeated routes are needed because a parked view can hide rebakes writing the same bytes.

The linked examples/vehicle-playground/authoring/ee-probes-2026-09-16/README.md is absent in this checkout. Those facts are preserved in docs/ee-submission-rearchitecture.md lines 336-409 and docs/backlog.md lines 550-574; the archived probe's raw assets were not independently rechecked here.

## Lifetime, cache and ordering requirements

1. SPR is 16 KiB of staging, not two frame stores. At most 1,024 qwords fit before reserving bookkeeping or a second staging window. A 128 KiB prefix is up to eight full 16 KiB transfers, or sixteen 8 KiB double-buffered transfers; no whole-prefix-in-SPR assumption is legal.
2. Reserve scratchpad ranges and DMA channel 8 explicitly. Refuse/fall back when a custom user already owns them; do not call dma_reset or unconditionally reinitialize a shared channel.
3. EE stores and compiler ordering must complete before fromSPR starts; confirm the SDK/manual barrier sequence. A C++ memory clobber is not itself a hardware barrier or write-back.
4. Keep each SPR chunk unchanged until its own fromSPR completion. Chunk completion permits SPR reuse. It does NOT permit RAM destination reuse while VIF1 still reads that frame.
5. Complete ALL fromSPR writes to the frame bank before publishing its VIF1 TADR. Do not extend a chain already executing, and do not patch END into NEXT.
6. DMA writes to ordinary RAM are not coherent with cached aliases. Destination lines must not retain dirty cached content that a later global flush writes over the staged prefix. Establish clean/invalidate destination ownership BEFORE DMA; prohibit cached writes after DMA. Guard CPU reads must use a proven alias/invalidation path. Preserve existing final FlushCache until this is demonstrated, including the risk that it overwrites a dirty destination alias.
7. Snapshot data, normal-mode GIF data copied by inlineVif, borrowed oversized direct sends, initial/foreign packets and newly built immutable cached spans still need publication. Staging only prefix tags cannot remove their flush requirements. Immutable means no mutation during a lease, not already in RAM.
8. Keep bankSequences/immutable reader masks and wrap-safe logical source fences unchanged. A newly built native prefix/snapshot invalidates any prior flushedUpTo coverage. A no-flush path needs a per-publication state, not an assumed once-per-bank flag.
9. Preserve VU FLUSHE/FLUSH/FLUSHA, GIF path ordering, GS presentation FINISH and VRAM final-reader lifetime. EE cache coherency, VIF1 DMA completion, VU execution completion and GS texture completion are four separate obligations.
10. The 1.169.1 post-presentation direct channel wait stays mandatory. A staged-send fallback must not reintroduce the callback/GIF-copy race or pending-new-HUD dependency.
11. Operations may cross chunk boundaries, but only committed byte ranges may be published. Current writer checkpoints/rewind can roll back an operation; flushing a tentative chunk early makes rollback impossible unless RAM cursor/state and staged data are transactional too. A prototype can avoid this by staging a finalized prefix first.
12. Prefix/source capacity overflow and allocation/channel refusal must preserve current synchronous behavior and counters. SPR wrap is not permission to overwrite unread data.

## Source publication ledger to build before no-flush

For every actual DMA-readable span, record physical start/end, writer/owner, generation, dirty/publication method, source fence and last reader. Enumerate native prefix, bank snapshot inline payloads, copied mutable REF arrays, newly minted immutable baked VIF streams, program uploads (MPG), texture IMAGE data, HUD/DIRECT data, normal GIF copies and direct borrowed fallback. Include source-to-snapshot CPU copies separately: CPU cache visibility during that copy does not mean DMAC sees the destination.

Registration must either prove once-per-generation publication or publish on first borrow. Content-version changes create a new generation; retired entries cannot be reused because two frame ticks elapsed. Trace writer ranges as well as REF ranges under --keep-routes/moving-camera tests. Keep diagnostic logging outside timing builds, since prints already masked a physical DMA race.

## Minimal independently testable prototype

P0: host-only staged-prefix storage model with aligned committed chunks, final END reservation, rollback, exact ordered-word oracle, delayed transfer completion, delayed VIF1-bank completion, two-bank leases and overflow/refusal. Use existing frame writer tests as baseline; add 1,023/1,024/1,025-qword boundaries, multi-chunk UNPACK/DIRECT/MPG, rollback crossing a boundary, and source mutation after commit. This can validate bookkeeping; it cannot test caches or EE/DMAC barriers.

P1: private scratch engine/game, finalized native prefix copied into a reserved SPR window, then fromSPR to clean frame-owned RAM in bounded chunks. Retain the RAM writer, current snapshot path, immutable leases and global FlushCache. A synchronized post-finalization copy is deliberately a correctness/overhead arm, not expected to improve performance. Guard compares staged destination bytes using a proven uncached/invalidation read before VIF1 begins. This isolates the new channel and bank lifecycle from producer rewrite and no-flush changes.

P2: replace prefix construction with committed SPR chunks, keep other source publication unchanged. Address rewind semantics explicitly, remove redundant cached-prefix writes, compare byte-stream oracle and measure construction/copy/fromSPR wait independently. Keep one final END and current fallback behavior. Only try double-buffered SPR chunks if single-window timing proves a staging stall worth overlapping.

P3: first no-global-flush arm only after the ledger proves all remaining RAM sources explicitly published and cached-destination aliases safe. Controls should include current cached+flush, staged+flush, staged+explicit-payload-publication+proven-barrier, plus deliberate source dirtiness cases. Do not run uncontrolled corrupt versions as performance candidates.

A concrete narrower P0 experiment was subsequently implemented in finalized-prefix-staging.cpp. It uses the ACTUAL repository FrameVifWriter to generate and finalize prefixes, then reconstructs those committed bytes through host windows. It does not invent a prospective streaming writer or validate rollback after staging has begun. P1-P3 require later exclusive console access and a private engine cache.

## The approximately 16-qword-plus-CALL object scheme

This is a useful target for low per-draw work, not a Tyra ABI or guarantee of an exact packet size. Current bag headers may include light state, clip planes, ALPHA/options, env/billboard basis or wrap operations, so fixed 16-qword uniform packets are not established. Need a current per-class prefix census before choosing a target.

Keep existing REF replay initially. A raw prebaked VIF span cannot be the target of DMA CALL: CALL would interpret its bytes as DMA tags. A CALL alternative requires a separately constructed subchain ending RET, validated target extents, bounded return-stack depth, recursion/cycle rejection, complete leased lifetime for nested REF payloads, explicit TTE command order and parser/arena support. It still must retain per-package visibility and VU uniform barriers. Host CALL/RET traversal could be prototyped independently, but no evidence currently shows it saves EE work beyond one REF replay. Prefer measuring why bags miss whole-bag replay, current uniform construction cost and native conversion cost before adding a second replay format.

## Acceptance and measurements

Correctness gates: ordered-word equality, full chain validation, exact staged-byte equality on EE, adversarial dirty-cache aliases, partial last chunks, allocation/channel refusal, bank wrap/reuse, retired immutable generations, cold/new baked entries, moving vehicles/lights, routes/streaming, procedural/dense transitions, repeated scene loads, HUD/textures, postfx/aux targets, display/pipeline/limiter toggles, readback and oversized fallback. Run quiet physical controls as well as guarded diagnostics. PCSX2 proves stream/pixel behavior only; it does not prove EE cache correctness.

Performance gates: same production ELF within each repeat, two fresh boots each arm/pose, unchanged camera/video/quality/input, aligned 512 raw work samples and neighboring full-period samples, guards/counters off. Report mean/median/p95, over-budget work, complete period, prefix qwords/frame, stage bytes/transfers/waits, source-copy bytes, write-back calls/ticks, warm versus cold behavior, fallback/split count and free RAM. Profile prefix construction and publication separately to avoid attributing all work reduction to cache flushing. Do not reuse S1's old 1.09 ms as a current ceiling, sum night effect-removal gains, call a CPU bracket full FPS or use emulator speed as PS2 evidence.

Success means preserved pixels, ownership and ordinary single-chain frames with lower physical critical-path work AND honest full-period reporting, bounded RAM and no regressions in the above stress cases. If staging adds cost or cache flush is already negligible after one-chain recording, close the experiment rather than ship complexity for resemblance to another title.

## Completed finalized-prefix host experiment

GCC 16.1.0 (installed MinGW) compiled the scratch harness with C++17, O2, Wall/Wextra/Werror and static linking. Result: PASS, 40 staging cases, 16,188 assertions, 124 completed host copies, 449 expected premature-write/publication/reuse refusals. This is finite coverage, not a general correctness proof.

Actual FrameVifWriter prefixes of 1, 511, 512, 513, 1023, 1024, 1025, 2049 and 8192 qwords exercised 8 KiB/16 KiB windows with one or two host staging slots. Short final chunks, independent 0xdeadbeef canaries and exact memcmp reconstruction passed. A mixed prefix contains NUM=0 UNPACK, a 2304-qword DIRECT spanning staging boundaries, NUM=0 MPG and a real REF emitted by the writer. A prior 2400-qword tentative DIRECT is rolled back through the actual writer API BEFORE finalization; only surviving committed bytes are staged. Every reconstructed chain passes the actual existing VIF validator.

The host model delays completion, rejects overwriting a held window, refuses publishing until every transfer completes, rejects rewriting a published bank, and retains two independent bank reader holds until explicitly released. The model compares against actual finalized bytes; its bank/window state machine is test scaffolding, not an implemented EE storage owner. REF payloads remain external: this test preserves the REF address, but does not snapshot or prove their cache/lifetime publication.

First compile exposed a misleading-indentation warning, corrected without reducing warnings. First dynamically linked executable failed before main with Windows exit -1073741511 (entry-point resolution); static linking ran successfully. No sanitizer was run. Source, static executable, build command/compiler record, result log and artifact hashes are preserved locally. No hardware, emulator, shared engine cache or repository files were used or changed.
